question: A charge of 1.5 C is moved through a potential difference. If the work done is 30 J , what is the potential difference between the two points?
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **work done (W)**, **charge (Q)**, and **potential difference (V)** is given by the formula: **V = W/Q**.
 
• Here, the work done **(W)** is given as **30 J**, and the charge **(Q)** is **1.5 C**.
 
• Using the formula: **V = W/Q = 30 J / 1.5 C = 20 V**.
 
• Therefore, the **potential difference** between the two points is **20 V**. The calculation is correct based on the given values.
 
• **Option 4: 20 V** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Potential Difference:**

 
 
• The potential difference is the work done in moving a unit charge from one point to another in an electric field.
 
• It is measured in **volts (V)**, where 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb.
 
• Potential difference is a scalar quantity and is represented mathematically as **V = W/Q**.
 
 
 
• **Work Done in Electric Fields:**
 
 
• Work done refers to the energy required to move a charge against an electric field.
 
• It is given by **W = Q × V**, where **Q** is the charge and **V** is the potential difference.
 
• The SI unit of work is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Charge:**
 
 
• Charge is a fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience a force in an electric field.
 
• It is measured in **coulombs (C)**, where 1 coulomb is the charge transported by a current of 1 ampere in 1 second.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potential Difference:**
 
 
• **Electrical Circuits:** Potential difference drives current through circuits, powering devices like lights, motors, and appliances.
 
• **Electrochemical Processes:** It is crucial in batteries and electroplating, where chemical reactions are driven by electric potential differences.
 
• **Measurement:** Devices like voltmeters measure the potential difference across components in electrical circuits.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formula Recap:** Always remember the formula **V = W/Q** for calculating potential difference, where **W** is in joules and **Q** is in coulombs.
 
• **Units:**
 
 
• The unit of potential difference is **volt (V)**, work is **joules (J)**, and charge is **coulombs (C)**.
 
• 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb.
 
 
 
• **Practical Example:** The potential difference of a standard AA battery is approximately **1.5 V**, while a car battery typically has a potential difference of **12 V**.
 
• When solving problems, ensure consistent units (e.g., joules, coulombs) to avoid calculation errors.
